49666735.article_summary: 文章称，2026年5月，疑似由OpenAI智能体群在RubyGems上传逾2000个恶意包，试图窃取用户API密钥，并利用RubyDoc.info执行任意代码。RubyGems因此暂停注册、删除相关包。攻击包多含“oai”标识，主要抓取英国地方政府公开信息，真实目的及是否成功尚不明确。
49666735.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 OpenAI 被指利用 AI agent 攻击 RubyGems、却未主动披露事件，评论者质疑其安全治理、责任承担及监管必要性。

不同观点：
• 信息隐瞒立场：OpenAI此前在 Hugging Face 事件和 Wiki 事件中已有披露机会，却未说明 RubyGems 事件；有人认为这是刻意隐瞒，甚至怀疑仍有更多未公开事件。  
• 能力与管理失控立场：OpenAI可能无法及时审查训练日志、识别攻击来源，或发现后因尴尬而沉默；这意味着其安全监控和内部控制严重不足。  
• 恶意竞争立场：反复“被抓到才披露”与对能力的高调宣传并存，可能是有意装无能，以此为监管壁垒、压制竞争。  
• 责任追究立场：评论者主张追究高管、董事会乃至刑事责任，暂停 OpenAI 的后续训练，并由 RubyGems 起诉、向受害开源项目赔偿。  
• 责任归属立场：不应把责任归于模糊的“agents”；无论是模型、机器人还是软件，最终责任主体都是 OpenAI。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 OpenAI 是“不知情、能力不足”，还是“明知却故意不披露”；评论也批评社会长期给予科技公司过度宽容，并指出开源社区难以公平应对大型 AI 实验室的攻击。

data.title: A misalignment of AI in mathematics
data.author: meredydd
data.article_summary: 文章指出，AI快速解决数学难题虽令人瞩目，却可能偏离数学追求概念理解、创新洞见与知识传承的根本目标。仓促发布、缺乏论证和署名还会引发抄袭与归属争议。作者认为，这反映了AI与学术及其他创造性工作的普遍错位，呼吁数学界、科技公司和社会尽快制定规范，确保AI服务于而非破坏人类的理解与创造。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI大规模参与数学及知识生产后，是否会削弱人类的理解、研究动力、学术评价与知识传承。

不同观点：
• 担忧派认为，AI直接给出答案会使“解题”与理解、洞察脱钩，削弱学生和研究者做实验、探索的意义；若荣誉、奖金和职业机会被AI公司夺走，人类从事纯粹数学的动力可能消失，并造成更广泛的知识劳动危机。  
• 乐观派认为，AI如同计算机之于国际象棋，能提供可靠答案，促使人类总结更深洞见。即使出现难以理解的AI证明，也可能引发会议、讲解、推广和新问题，推动数学发展。  
• 现实调整派认为，AI未必摧毁理解能力，却会摧毁以“率先解决开放问题”为核心的贡献尺度，导致抢先发表、保密竞争，或转向更主观、易争议的署名和评价制度。  
• 技术务实派认为数学可能分化为“理解的、无法理解的、虽不理解但可验证的”三类；不应仅因人类跟不上就限制AI，但需警惕认知债务、糟糕抽象和无反馈的“绕过困难”。  
• 批判派质疑AI公司的目标与公共利益一致，认为其可能牺牲数学家、程序员及弱势国家，扩大不平等；也有人以摄影、电话接线员和编程自动化说明技术变革并非首次带来职业冲击。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于数学的首要价值究竟是正确结果还是人类理解过程，以及社会应限制AI、适应新评价机制，还是接受机器主导的知识生产。

49662371.article_content:
A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics
Over the last few months, the mathematical capabilities of LLMs have improved dramatically, to the point that they can solve major outstanding problems in many fields of mathematics. However, the push by AI companies to solve mathematical problems as a benchmark is detrimental to the science of mathematics, and to the mathematical community. The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned. We see these as part of broader alignment issues impacting other scientific and creative professions, as well as the whole of society.
Research mathematics deals with understanding basic structures of shapes, numbers, and natural phenomena. Over the course of generations, it has built a large corpus of sophisticated ideas, methods, abstractions, and other tools to comprehend the mathematical landscape. In turn, modern technologies and sciences are based on mathematical tools.
Famous problems have often served as landmarks and lighthouses against which one can measure an improved understanding of this landscape. Solving one of these problems has been a certain sign of new insights and interesting methods, which would then be studied by a community of mathematicians, through a long and arduous process of talks, discussions, simplifications. At the end of this process, one will ideally find a textbook presentation of the results suitable for any graduate or even undergraduate student to study. Some of the mathematical ideas pursue their journey even further to become, decades or centuries after, tools that are understood and used by the whole population.
The mathematical community functions, in many ways, as a miniature version of humanity. It consists of individuals using a wide variety of different approaches, joined by core values. The most precious resources of our profession are students and ideas, and these we nurture with great care. We feel responsible to let them grow to their full potential, until they can live a life of their own in the mathematical world. For students we often suggest problems with the core intention of developing skills making them well-positioned for advances in research and elsewhere. Our ideas we disseminate in talks, private discussions and careful writeups, connecting them to the previous ideas of others. These processes invariably take time and are based on human interaction.
In recent months, the success of AI in solving major mathematical problems has made headlines even outside mathematical circles. But solving problems is only a tool and proxy for achieving the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight. Forgetting this in the world of AI may turn the tool against the primary goal. Indeed, the mass production at faster and faster pace of "true/false" statements could destroy fertile ground instead of breathing life into new ideas.
Often these solutions are announced in a rush, leaving no time for a proper writeup, the isolation of new methods and ideas, and citing relevant previous work of others. As in all creative professions, this raises severe attribution and plagiarism questions. Moreover, without the willing mathematicians who must take care of their development and integration into the mathematical canon, AI-conceived ideas would never become fully alive and the crucial human transmission chain between mathematicians would be lost.
We are witnessing a general threat to intellectual work, with misalignment between the outcome of the use of AI and its initial purpose. In many fields and activities, years of training have traditionally served not only to produce a final answer or product, but also to develop understanding and the ability to formulate new questions and ideas. However, building on a vast body of previous human work, AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of producing the results of such work directly, and these goals cease to align. The issues the mathematical community faces now are similar to issues that other scientific and creative professions are facing, and indicate issues that all of humanity might face: how to make sure that, as AI changes the way work is done, we do not lose sight of what that work was meant to achieve in the first place.
AI offers the potential of enhancing and accelerating genuine mathematical study and understanding. Mathematics as a profession will need to adapt to these changes in several ways. However, whether these changes ultimately benefit the field or have a destructive effect will in large part be determined by the decisions of the humans in control of this new technology.
These issues must be addressed urgently, in the mathematical community, by the companies developing these technologies and, more broadly, by a society that will confront similar problems in many other forms of intellectual work.

data.title: Show HN: ResolveHQ – A Helpdesk Built on Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2 and Queues
data.author: mirza_rizvi
data.article_summary: ResolveHQ 是一款基于 Cloudflare 的可自托管帮助台，面向小型客服团队，提供共享收件箱、工单管理、客户隔离、邮件收发、附件、知识库、报表、自动化、通知及 AI 草拟回复等功能。它采用 Worker、D1、R2、Queues 和 Email Routing 构建，支持多组织、角色权限、数据导出与删除、邮件重试及工单保留策略，可在 Cloudflare 免费计划上运行，并通过 Resend 发送邮件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：项目的可用性展示、自托管客服系统的价值，以及其能否替代现有客服工具。

不同观点：
• 展示不足：orliesaurus和14u2c都认为README缺少功能截图，且没有演示站，会降低用户理解和尝试项目的意愿。  
• 自托管的成本与价值：robgough认可自托管客服平台的需求，指出传统工具升级成本高，但也推广了自己的产品，强调客户门户、更新日志、路线图、监控和事件管理等更完整的功能。  
• 技术方案值得肯定：gepeake分享了使用Cloudflare Workers和Resend搭建邮件客户端的经验，认为Workers在邮件路由和快速创建域名邮箱方面很实用，但这属于相关技术的延伸讨论。  
• 替代现有工具的期待：roflchoppa直接提出核心诉求，希望项目能够替代或“干掉”Jira，反映出用户对迁移成本和功能完整性的关注。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在于项目展示和功能成熟度是否足以吸引用户，以及轻量、自托管方案与商业化、功能更全面的平台之间如何取舍。

ResolveHQ
ResolveHQ is a Cloudflare-native, self-hostable helpdesk for small support teams.
What you can do
Run a shared inbox with tenant-isolated customers, tickets, assignment, status, priority, tags, and full-text search.
Sign up as owner, invite teammates, and manage Owner/Admin/Agent roles with a workspace switcher across organizations.
Thread email correctly per RFC 5322, resistant to subject-line spoofing across tickets.
Receive mail through Cloudflare Email Routing and send it through Resend, with delivery status, retries, and idempotent webhooks. Outbound replies carry their linked attachments, and dead-letter queues drain to durable, recoverable records.
Attach files to tickets through validated, authorized R2 uploads.
Reply faster with saved replies, internal notes, AI-drafted responses (opt-in), and a responsive three-pane inbox with optimistic-version conflict handling.
Reset passwords and accept invitations through system email sent via the same provider seam as ticket mail.
Publish a public help center from knowledge-base articles, with drafts kept private to your team.
Track volume and response speed in Reports, export any window to CSV, and automate triage with rule-based Automations.
Notify agents of assignments and customer replies in-app, and work comfortably in light or dark mode.
Export everything stored about a customer as JSON, or erase it with a durable, resumable workflow that cancels queued mail.
Recover automatically: a five-minute cron job retries stalled mail jobs and cleans up staging and orphaned data.
Control AI assistance per workspace: it stays off until an admin enables it in Settings, and only then are ticket conversations sent to OpenAI.
Set
TICKET_RETENTION_DAYS
(for example
365
) to have the scheduled sweep permanently delete resolved and closed tickets older than that window, including attachments.
Interface
The workspace uses a Slack-inspired aubergine sidebar, self-hosted Lato typography, Lucide icons, and Radix UI primitives. Theme-aware controls and status colors support light and dark workspaces. On mobile, bottom navigation and a keyboard-accessible workspace drawer keep all destinations available; ticket columns adapt to preserve subject readability.
Use
Cmd/Ctrl+K
to jump between pages. The sidebar dock contains notifications, theme switching, and account actions.
How it works
ResolveHQ runs as a single Cloudflare Worker in your own account. Hono serves both the REST API and the built React application. Cloudflare D1 holds tickets and customers, Cloudflare R2 holds attachments, and Cloudflare Queues carry inbound and outbound mail jobs. Cloudflare Email Routing delivers incoming mail to the Worker, and Resend sends outgoing mail. Tickets and attachments are stored in your Cloudflare account; outbound email content passes through Resend.
How much does it cost?
ResolveHQ can run on Cloudflare’s Free plan for small deployments, provided usage stays within the current limits for Workers, D1, R2, Queues, Cron Triggers, and Email Routing. CPU-intensive authentication or mail parsing may require Workers Paid; benchmark your deployment. Queues are available on Workers Free. R2 requires account activation and billing setup separately. Resend handles outbound email under its own limits. See the
Free-plan audit
.
Deploy
The easiest way to get started is with the
Deploy to Cloudflare
button above. You will need:
A Cloudflare account; Workers Free supports Queues. Activate R2 separately.
A domain on Cloudflare, so you can set up Email Routing.
Optionally, a Resend account with a verified sending domain, to send outgoing mail.
After deployment, open your ResolveHQ URL and sign up as the owner, giving an optional support email that becomes your default inbox. In the Cloudflare dashboard, add an Email Routing rule sending that address to the dep

• 自托管的成本与价值：robgough认可自托管客服平台的需求，指出传统工具升级成本高，但也推广了自己的产品，强调客户门户、更新日志、路线图、监控和事件管理等更完整的功能。  
• 技术方案值得肯定：gepeake分享了使用Cloudflare Workers和Resend搭建邮件客户端的经验，认为Workers在邮件路由和快速创建域名邮箱方面很实用，但这属于相关技术的延伸讨论。  
• 替代现有工具的期待：roflchoppa直接提出核心诉求，希望项目能够替代或“干掉”Jira，反映出用户对迁移成本和功能完整性的关注。

data.title: Litelm: LiteLLM Without the Bloat
data.author: kennethwolters
data.article_summary: Litelm 是一个轻量级 Python 库，提取 LiteLLM 的核心调用能力，仅约 2900 行代码、依赖 OpenAI 和 HTTPX。它支持多模型提供商路由、消息格式转换、流式输出、工具调用、嵌入、文本补全及 Responses API，并提供异步接口。相比 LiteLLM，移除了代理、缓存、计费、路由器等复杂功能，适合追求简洁的应用，也兼容 OpenAI API 格式及本地模型服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕精简版 LiteLLM 的定位、功能取舍、项目质量及 LLM 基础设施的长期价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持精简方向：认为用 LLM 从开源项目中提取核心功能很有价值，减少代码量和依赖有助于提高效率；但 README 还应说明是否带来更低延迟、更低内存等实际收益。
• 反对过度删减：成本追踪、流式响应、缓存等功能正是 LiteLLM 的核心价值，尤其适合按客户统计跨服务 Token 支出；因此“无臃肿”这一定位受到质疑。
• 主张可扩展设计：建议提供插件或扩展机制，让用户自行实现缓存、成本计算等功能。
• 质疑项目质量与必要性：有人认为 README 像是由 AI 生成，建议人工重写；也有人认为这是前沿 LLM 生成的短时项目，技术方法比具体库更有价值，甚至可直接调用 LLM 或自行编写客户端。
• 其他比较：有人推荐自制客户端并认为质量更高，也有人询问其与 Bifrost 的差异；另有评论指出依赖的 `httpx` 维护状况存在问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“轻量化”应否牺牲 LiteLLM 的核心基础设施能力，以及一个小型衍生库能否提供足够长期、可靠的价值。

data.title: Testing Race Conditions
data.author: alpaylan
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了用于探索多线程竞态条件的 Linux 内核工具集 MAccConc。该项目通过记录内存访问、识别可能互相影响的通信点，自动或手动探索线程交错，从而帮助确认竞态漏洞、编写可靠回归测试并辅助模糊测试。工具提供自动测试 A-B-A 交错、终端界面和图形界面，灵感来自 SKI 等并发测试研究。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

49634928.article_content:
Many security bugs are race conditions, where multi-threaded execution has to occur with the right interleaving for a negative effect to appear. This creates challenges for several use cases:
Confirming bug candidates that have been discovered manually or through static analysis.
Regression tests: After fixing a race condition bug, there is often no good way to write a regression test that reliably triggers the bug as part of a test suite.
Automatic bug discovery, such as fuzzing: It is hard for a fuzzer to exercise all interesting interleavings of concurrent operations, or reach code paths that are only exercised when operations are racing.
I mostly discover bugs by manually reading code. When I think Iâve found a bug, I normally write a test case to either prove or disprove that the bug exists. For race condition bugs, it can be hard to achieve either outcome. For Linux kernel bugs, I often resort to recompiling the kernel after adding conditional
mdelay()
calls (which spinloop for roughly the specified amount of time) in appropriate places; I usually make these conditional based on the name of the running thread, though sometimes more complex conditions are needed. On platforms that support DTrace (like macOS and
Windows
), it is possible to use DTrace probes that call
chill()
for similar effect, though the utility of this is limited as DTrace can only trace on non-inline function boundaries or explicit trace points, rather than on every instruction. Regardless of platform, this approach can be time consuming and can require trial and error to definitely determine whether code is buggy.
Additionally, in the Linux kernel, fixes for race condition bugs are often accompanied by hand-written ASCII diagrams showing problematic thread interleavings with call graphs and relevant memory accesses (for example, see this recent
rt_spin_unlock UAF fix
, or this recent
jbd2 deadlock fix
). It would be convenient to have developer tooling that can analyze potentially vulnerable code and show results in a similar representation.
Summary
I wrote tools for exploring possible interleavings of multi-threaded test cases for the Linux kernel:
A tool that automatically tests all possible A-B-A interleavings of a test case.
A terminal UI for manual exploration of possible interleavings.
A GUI for manual exploration of possible interleavings.
The kernel part of this is intended to also be usable for discovering race conditions via fuzzing, but userspace tooling for that still needs to be implemented.
The tools are available
on GitHub
under the name MAccConc, short for âMemory Access Concurrencyâ; see the README there for installation and usage instructions.
If you just want to see the tooling in action, skip to
Demo: automatic testing
.
If youâre just interested in the theory behind the tooling, read section
Stable identifiers for memory accesses across runs: count-augmented stack traces
.
Prior work
This project was inspired by discussions with Ned Williamson, whose
sockfuzzer
project involved exploration of concurrency bugs by using a custom scheduler that can reschedule at synchronization primitives to explore interleavings. See the conference talk
slides
and
recording
focused on the concurrency testing aspect of this.
My tooling is largely based on ideas similar to
SKI
, but SKI uses a different implementation: It records memory accesses and controls scheduling of vCPUs using a patched version of QEMU in TCG mode, and uses VM snapshots to explore different execution interleavings.
Discovering memory accesses that could contribute to race conditions (communication points)
As described in the SKI paper, interesting execution interleavings of a given multi-threaded test case can be discovered by tracing memory accesses of all threads and searching for pairs of accesses on two threads that could interact with each other - meaning, roughly, that at least one of them is a write operation, and they access overlapping memory ranges. The SKI paper calls such memory accesses
communication points
.
This requires some mechanism to collect memory access coverage. SKI did this by patching QEMUâs TCG mode; I am instead relying on ASAN instrumentation in âoutlineâ mode (compiler backend flag
asan-instrumentation-with-call-threshold=0
, selected by
CONFIG_KASAN_OUTLINE
in the Linux kernel), which generates helper function calls on memory access. I believe that the kernel is the right place to collect this data because it would allow the kernel to also provide higher-level information about lock acquire/release events and such, though I have not implemented this at this time. Implementing this in the kernel also means that it would theoretically be possible to test on bare-metal hardware, rather than inside VMs.
Since Linux already has
KCOV
as a mechanism to feed basic block kernel coverage information to userspace, I decided to use the same mechanism to record information about memory accesses. An alternative would have been t

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：讨论 Project Blinkenlights 及其城市灯光装置的知名度、文化影响和技术实现，核心是怀旧、致敬与项目传播方式。

不同观点：
• 经典怀旧派：认为这是“互联网老兵”式的经典项目；有人回忆在柏林亚历山大广场看到装置，并用诺基亚手机玩 Pong，也有人提到柏林 Chaos Computer Club 和 Tim，赞赏其黑客精神与“艺术的可能性”。
• 技术与城市装置派：指出深圳市中心、旧金山海湾大桥等地也曾采用类似灯光系统；评论者还介绍了受 Blinkenlights 启发的 BlinkenCity，利用可远程控制的街灯构成全城互动装置。
• 相关项目联想派：有人联想到终端中的 ASCII《星球大战》服务 `towel.blinkenlights.nl`，也有人回忆多伦多 City Hall 的 Stereoscope（96×32像素、16级灰度）。
• 质疑传播效果派：认为该项目可能遭遇“HN kiss of death”，即在 Hacker News 获得关注后反而因页面扩展性、适配能力不足而影响体验，并提出应讨论如何避免类似问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在于项目如今是否仍被广泛认识，以及其经典地位与网页技术表现之间的落差。

data.article_summary: Google DeepMind推出“AlphaGenome Atlas”，可预测约90亿种单碱基DNA变异对基因表达和调控的影响。该工具有助于识别与疾病相关的遗传变化，推动基因组研究和生物医学发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Google 发布相关科学成果的宣传力度，以及这些成果的实际影响和后续研究方向展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [tusimi]认为，Google 正在大力宣传影响相对有限的科学成果，暗示其宣传效果超过了成果本身的重要性，带有“公关机器”运作的意味。  
• [samuell]提出应进一步研究这些成果之间的组合效果，即不要只分别分析单项成果，也要关注它们结合后是否能产生更高价值或突破。  
• [epistasis]通过链接此前讨论，暗示当前评论应放在先前帖子的背景下理解，可能是在延续关于这些科学成果及其意义的讨论。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“宣传声势”与“实际科学影响”是否匹配。评论者一方质疑成果的现实价值，另一方则把注意力转向成果组合后可能产生的潜在价值。不过，由于未提供链接帖子的具体内容，无法进一步判断“它们”具体指哪些成果。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：论文提出将查询优化器作为服务，讨论其工程实用性、SQL作为中间表示（IR）的合理性，以及其中“AI”实现的透明度与实际价值。

不同观点：
• remywang认为这种“查询优化器即服务”的思路很实用，但质疑数据库领域把SQL固定为中间表示，认为这一设计令人不适或存在局限。
• schultzer持保留态度：论文和官网没有清楚说明工作机制，论文似乎描述传统优化器，官网却强调AI，可能存在宣传夸大甚至“AI包装”的问题。
• schultzer同时承认该想法可能很有价值，但前提是它确实实现了专门的优化引擎，而不是把统计信息直接复制到聊天机器人中生成建议。

补充讨论：评论之间的核心争议不是概念是否有趣，而是实现是否真实、技术细节是否充分，以及AI是否带来了超越传统方法的实际能力。

data.title: Rune is now open source
data.author: ernestrc
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Go 开发的终端化 IDE Rune，讨论其创新理念、上手体验、技术路线、协作机制及产品完善方向。

不同观点：
• 认可其终端优先、跨平台和可编程理念：终端可发送鼠标等事件，支持窗口、任务栏集成，并能回退到 TTY、SSH 或 Docker 环境；有人赞赏命令提示的可发现性、`go run` 即可运行，以及 Go 构建编辑器的实践。
• 认为 Rune 仍有较高上手门槛：Vim 用户开启 Vim 模式后几乎无法操作， onboarding 变成强制训练，导致用户直接卸载；建议降低尝试成本或明确警告。
• 对协作与商业模式意见分化：有人赞赏开放账本和贡献者分成，认为比 CLA 更具创新；也有人担心金钱激励带来类似 Hacktoberfest、AI 垃圾 PR 的刷贡献问题。
• 对安全和基础设施存疑：用户希望不依赖协调服务器及其加密方案，建议支持 Tailscale 或 SSH 直连。
• 对产品成熟度提出改进需求：主题选择较差，尤其缺少 Solarized、Gruvbox 和浅色主题；希望增加演示视频、Fedora 软件包，并明确键盘驱动是否支持普通非模态编辑。
• 对生态和定位持谨慎态度：有人将其视为 Zed、VSCode 或 zellij 的替代品，但仍在观望；指出 TypeScript 用户群庞大，Rune 需要优先支持 TS。

补充讨论：评论整体认可项目潜力，但争议集中在“创新是否牺牲易用性”、贡献者分成的激励副作用，以及集中式协作服务的信任问题。

data.title: Λ Snap – An inviting programming language for kids and adults for CS study
data.author: dr_kiszonka
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Snap!，这是一个面向儿童和成人的编程语言及计算机科学学习平台。页面提供“立即运行”、示例项目和学习资源，并展示了用户创作的精选作品，涵盖游戏、艺术、计算机科学和模拟实验等类别，同时收录 Snap!Con 2025 项目及更多作品合集。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Scratch/Snap 等积木式编程工具的教育价值、表达能力、可维护性及未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• Scratch 适合入门且能培养编程兴趣。有人从 Scratch 起步并进入软件行业，但项目达到约1万积木后会严重卡顿，促使其开发 goboscript，说明其适合启蒙却存在规模限制。  
• Snap! 比 Scratch 更强大，支持自定义积木、一等列表、过程和延续，适合中学或大学计算机教育，也能较直观地教授 Scheme。  
• Snap! 的代价是复杂度和稳定性：改名可能造成调用处“空洞”且不报错，调试困难；积木散落在画布上，项目变大后难以查找和组织，传统 IDE/文件结构可能更好。  
• 反对者认为积木环境虽能教编程，却难以教软件工程；复杂到一定程度后，积木的优势减弱。MakeCode 被认为比 Snap! 更简单、更容易让孩子接受。  
• 图形化工具仍有硬件和创意教育价值，例如 LEGO WeDo、机器人、刺绣和 AI 编程等，但需要关注兼容性及官方软件停更问题。  
• 也有人质疑今天是否还需要教儿童编程，暗示教育目标和必要性本身仍有争议。

补充讨论：Snap! 可通过键盘操作和 Scheme 互译增强可用性；但在 AI 代码生成方面，JavaScript 因普及度和文本表达效率明显优于积木语言。

49662214.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Snap!，这是一个面向儿童和成人的编程语言及计算机科学学习平台。页面提供“立即运行”、示例项目和学习资源，并展示了用户创作的精选作品，涵盖游戏、艺术、计算机科学和模拟实验等类别，同时收录 Snap!Con 2025 项目及更多作品合集。
49662214.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Scratch/Snap 等积木式编程工具的教育价值、表达能力、可维护性及未来发展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• Scratch 适合入门且能培养编程兴趣。有人从 Scratch 起步并进入软件行业，但项目达到约1万积木后会严重卡顿，促使其开发 goboscript，说明其适合启蒙却存在规模限制。  
• Snap! 比 Scratch 更强大，支持自定义积木、一等列表、过程和延续，适合中学或大学计算机教育，也能较直观地教授 Scheme。  
• Snap! 的代价是复杂度和稳定性：改名可能造成调用处“空洞”且不报错，调试困难；积木散落在画布上，项目变大后难以查找和组织，传统 IDE/文件结构可能更好。  
• 反对者认为积木环境虽能教编程，却难以教软件工程；复杂到一定程度后，积木的优势减弱。MakeCode 被认为比 Snap! 更简单、更容易让孩子接受。  
• 图形化工具仍有硬件和创意教育价值，例如 LEGO WeDo、机器人、刺绣和 AI 编程等，但需要关注兼容性及官方软件停更问题。  
• 也有人质疑今天是否还需要教儿童编程，暗示教育目标和必要性本身仍有争议。

补充讨论：Snap! 可通过键盘操作和 Scheme 互译增强可用性；但在 AI 代码生成方面，JavaScript 因普及度和文本表达效率明显优于积木语言。

data.author: miuraboy
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了日语赫本罗马字的作用、原则、历史与现状。该系统用拉丁字母标注日语发音，优先帮助英语使用者准确读音，因此“し”写作“shi”而非“si”。它由赫本及日本学者共同完善，1867年随日英词典推广，后成为教材、护照、道路和车站广泛采用的标准。2025年，日本政府正式将其确立为国家罗马字标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章对日语罗马字系统（尤其是赫本式、训令式、日文式）的介绍是否准确，以及初学者应如何学习。

不同观点：
• motionlessveloc认为文章总体正确，但忽略了关键历史背景：训令式等非赫本系统原本意在彻底替代日文文字，服务对象是日本人，因此无需迁就英语语音；汉语拼音也有类似目标，这解释了其字母用法对英语读者而言不直观。  
• rkido指出文章存在事实错误：训令式并非假名与字母一一对应，只有日文式具备这一特点。因此他认为日文式更适合严肃学习者；不过初学者通常最好直接学习假名，而不是依赖罗马字。  
• lyall质疑文章及其讨论的价值，认为文章明显像人工智能生成，内容质量却仍获得关注。他以“三个日语词对应三种赫本转写”为例，讽刺文章只是用熟悉字母标示发音，信息量有限。

补充讨论：评论之间的争议主要集中在文章的准确性与实用性。motionlessveloc和rkido是在纠正具体历史、技术细节，lyall则进一步质疑文章的可信度及读者为何关注它；各方总体都倾向于认为学习假名比长期依赖罗马字更重要。

Hepburn Romanization: How to Read Japanese in the Latin Alphabet
Technical

written by

There is a moment every learner of Japanese goes through. You see the word æ±äº¬ written on a sign, and it is beautiful, and you have no idea what it sounds like. The characters carry meaning and sound at the same time, but only if you already know them. Before you have studied kana and kanji, they are elegant drawings that tell you nothing about pronunciation.
Romanization serves as the bridge. It writes the sounds of Japanese in the Latin alphabet, the same twenty-six letters you are reading right now, so that someone who has never studied the language can sound out a word and get close to how a Japanese speaker would say it. And the system that does this job, the one your textbook uses, the one on Japanese road signs and train stations and passports, the one the entire internet defaults to, is Hepburn romanization.
The system is not new. An American missionary named James Curtis Hepburn popularized it in 1867, in the first Japanese-English dictionary, though the system itself was developed by the RÅmaji-kai (Romanization Club), a society of Japanese and foreign scholars of which Hepburn was a member. What is new is that in December 2025, the Japanese government made Hepburn the official national romanization standard, the first revision of the national rules in about seventy years. The system the world was already using is now the system Japan officially recommends.
1867
the year Hepburn's dictionary popularized the system
2025
the year Japan made it the national standard
5

Three Japanese words, three Hepburn transcriptions. The letters you already know, telling you what they sound like.
What Hepburn romanization actually is
#
Hepburn romanization is a system for transcribing Japanese sounds into the Latin alphabet, designed so that an English speaker reading the result will pronounce the word close to how a Japanese speaker would. That is the entire design principle, and every property of the system flows from it.
The principle comes with a trade-off. Hepburn is phonetic for English speakers, not systematic for kana. The syllable ã is written "shi" and not "si," because "shi" is closer to how ã sounds to an English reader. This is the core decision that defines Hepburn and drives every difference from its competitors. A system that maps kana to romanization in a regular, one-to-one way writes ã as "si," which is cleaner as a rule but misleading as a pronunciation guide. Hepburn chose pronunciation over consistency.
There are three variants worth knowing. Traditional Hepburn is the original system from the 1867 dictionary, which romanized some sounds in ways that have since been refined. Modified Hepburn, also called Revised Hepburn, is the modern standard: it regularized a few edge cases and is the version used in textbooks, passports, and most dictionaries. The third variation concerns macron usage, particularly whether the long "i" gets a macron (sensei vs sensÄ), which is a matter of style rather than a substantive difference.
The history: a dictionary, a missionary, and a society
#
James Curtis Hepburn was an American Presbyterian missionary and physician who arrived in Japan in 1859, one of the first Westerners to settle in Yokohama after the country opened to foreign trade. He was a doctor by training, but his lasting contribution was lexicographic. Over eight years, with the help of Japanese assistants, he compiled the first Japanese-English dictionary, published in 1867. The romanization system in that dictionary was a practical tool: it let English speakers look up Japanese words they could not yet read, and it let them pronounce what they found.
The dictionary went through multiple editions. The third edition, published in 1886, adopted the system refined by the RÅmaji-kai, the Romanization Society, a group of Japanese and foreign scholars who had been working on standardizing romanization. This is the version that became the standard and is essentially what we now call Modified Hepburn.
Hepburn was not alone. His chief assistant was Kishida GinkÅ, a Japanese scholar who contributed substantially to the dictionary and the romanization system. The collaboration is worth noting because it means Hepburn romanization, despite bearing an American name, was a joint Japanese-American project from the start.
The system spread through dictionaries, textbooks, and eventually into official use. By the mid-twentieth century it was the romanization on passports, road signs, and train station names. But it was never the official system of the Japanese government. That role belonged to Kunrei-shiki, a more systematic romanization made the national standard in 1937 and reaffirmed in 1954. data.title: Mind-altering drugs played key role in rise of Andean civilization
data.author: geneticdrifts
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：致幻剂在古代文明、艺术、宗教仪式及现代精神疾病治疗中的作用，以及其影响究竟是促进文明还是带来危险。

不同观点：
• **现代治疗与研究价值**：有人认为致幻剂的潜在疗效和风险早已受到使用者关注；随着社会观念转变、禁毒战争影响减弱，相关研究获得资金和学生支持，有望用于精神疾病治疗。  
• **艺术与象征体系的影响**：有评论认为，原住民陶器和建筑中的几何图案可能受曼陀罗等致幻植物影响，并推荐视频作为论据来源，但这一说法仍需更多考古证据。  
• **对文明起源作用的质疑**：有人指出，现代地下环境同样存在壁画和吸毒用具，仅凭类似现象，不能证明药物在文明兴起中发挥关键作用。  
• **广义文化促进作用**：另一观点认为，酒精等改变意识的物质也可能参与许多文明的发展，因此致幻剂未必特殊。  
• **意识起源假说**：有人推测，致幻剂通过改变默认模式网络、增强神经可塑性，可能促进意识形成，但目前属于推测，缺少直接证据。  
• **危险与权力**：反对者强调，致幻剂也可能服务于萨满权威、宗教控制和大规模祭祀杀人，不能只强调其治疗或启发作用。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于相关现象是因果证据还是文化伴随现象，以及致幻剂究竟主要带来创造性、治疗价值，还是操控与暴力风险。

data.title: I've operated petabyte-scale ClickHouse clusters for 5 years
data.author: adastral
data.article_summary: Tinybird是一款基于ClickHouse的托管数据平台，帮助团队快速接入数据、构建亚秒级SQL API和Kafka实时分析系统。平台提供面向AI与开发者的体验、安全模式迁移、零拷贝分支、基础设施监控及企业级集群管理与支持，适用于实时仪表盘、CDC、游戏和网页分析等场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ClickHouse 在高吞吐分析、摄取、存储架构与运维治理上的取舍。

不同观点：
• 运维治理派认为，高写入量和频繁变更需要 DBA 作为“守门人”，限制查询、Schema 和访问模式变更，降低风险；但用微服务替代 DBA 包装数据库，往往损失可靠性和直接访问带来的性能。
• 架构选择派认为，数据可先写入 Parquet/对象存储再读取，或按读写、部门、用户隔离，并结合 DuckDB；也有人希望 Amazon 提供 RDS 版以降低运维成本。
• ClickHouse 实践者指出其非常耗磁盘，且“too many parts”等摄取问题普遍存在，Kafka 可用于缓冲和背压。
• 质疑者反驳文章：原生 TCP 持久连接有助于降低低延迟查询成本；ClickHouse 依赖本地 NVMe 正是性能来源，对象存储会增加网络跳数；OLAP 的价值在于支持未知查询，不应只测试预设查询。

补充讨论：争议集中在低延迟与云存储弹性、实时摄取与批量写入、自由查询与治理成本之间的权衡；另有人询问 ClickHouse 与 Elasticsearch、Pinot、Trino、Spark 的定位，以及如何处理 `now()` 和近似聚合导致的回放结果差异。

49601138.article_summary: Tinybird是一款基于ClickHouse的托管数据平台，帮助团队快速接入数据、构建亚秒级SQL API和Kafka实时分析系统。平台提供面向AI与开发者的体验、安全模式迁移、零拷贝分支、基础设施监控及企业级集群管理与支持，适用于实时仪表盘、CDC、游戏和网页分析等场景。
49601138.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ClickHouse 在高吞吐分析、摄取、存储架构与运维治理上的取舍。

不同观点：
• 运维治理派认为，高写入量和频繁变更需要 DBA 作为“守门人”，限制查询、Schema 和访问模式变更，降低风险；但用微服务替代 DBA 包装数据库，往往损失可靠性和直接访问带来的性能。
• 架构选择派认为，数据可先写入 Parquet/对象存储再读取，或按读写、部门、用户隔离，并结合 DuckDB；也有人希望 Amazon 提供 RDS 版以降低运维成本。
• ClickHouse 实践者指出其非常耗磁盘，且“too many parts”等摄取问题普遍存在，Kafka 可用于缓冲和背压。
• 质疑者反驳文章：原生 TCP 持久连接有助于降低低延迟查询成本；ClickHouse 依赖本地 NVMe 正是性能来源，对象存储会增加网络跳数；OLAP 的价值在于支持未知查询，不应只测试预设查询。

补充讨论：争议集中在低延迟与云存储弹性、实时摄取与批量写入、自由查询与治理成本之间的权衡；另有人询问 ClickHouse 与 Elasticsearch、Pinot、Trino、Spark 的定位，以及如何处理 `now()` 和近似聚合导致的回放结果差异。

data.title: The EPA is planning to scrap public review rules for data center pollution
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 文章称，美国民众普遍反对在社区附近建设人工智能数据中心，但联邦环保政策拟削弱公众参与和许可监管，甚至允许项目获批前开工。数据中心及配套燃气电厂可能加剧空气污染、健康风险和电费上涨，且建设多集中于农村及黑人社区。地方政府与科技企业签署保密协议，也引发透明度和环境正义争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕EPA拟放宽数据中心环境审查、削弱公众参与及其对AI发展、地方治理和生态环境的影响展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 反对者认为这是环境监管倒退，EPA已被政府削弱，放宽规则将纵容环境破坏；有人讽刺其已变成“环境破坏保护机构”，并认为反对建设数据中心的社区因此得到印证。  
• 部分评论者认为，政府正以AI竞争和国家安全为由牺牲环保，类似冷战时期在本土进行核试验；但也有人警告，政策可能随政府更迭，企业不应据此作长期投资。  
• 支持地方裁量者指出，将公众参与的时间和方式交给州、地方机构并非必然有害，地方选举也最能体现民意；相关媒体报道可能靠耸动标题制造焦虑。  
• 另有观点认为公众讨论容易被情绪和社交媒体操纵，反对者常以“虚假论据”阻止数据中心；但也有人主张发展可持续数据中心，这本是美国企业和科研机构具备优势的重大机会。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于环境保护、公众参与应优先于建设效率，还是应为AI竞争和国家战略让路；评论者也质疑报道是否偏颇，并追问如何实际阻止政策变化。

49662672.article_content:
Attendees react during an April 25 public comment meeting hosted by the Shelby County Health Department on xAI's permit application to use gas turbines for a new data center in Memphis, Tennessee. (Brandon Dill for The Washington Post via Getty Images)
We Write the Untold Stories of Black America
Read them in Seen & Heard, our free, twice-weekly newsletter.
Sign up
Americans don’t agree on much, but that’s not the case when it comes to data centers.
​Seven in 10 Americans
oppose
building data centers for artificial intelligence in or near their communities. Despite this, the federal government is moving to make it easier for them to be built. And in some places, residents won’t even get the chance to raise concerns publicly or even know if a data center is coming to their neighborhoods.
The federal Environmental Protection Agency plans to scrap a federal requirement that states tell the public — and allow public comment — before approving air-pollution permits for industrial facilities. That includes the data centers rising across the country, as well as the power plants built to feed their enormous appetite for electricity.
At the same time, the EPA last month also proposed another change that would let developers start building data centers before their permits are approved.
The rural South, which is home to a disproportionate amount of Black communities, has seen the largest growth of these large data centers. The proposals and lack of transparency may worsen health risks, increase utility bills, and contribute to community displacement, residents told Capital B.
​The change at the federal level would mean that, in some places, residents could lose one of their few formal chances to ask questions, raise alarms, or learn that a data center is headed their way before the permits are signed and construction begins.
Paul Black, an environmental activist organizing against a data center complex the size of 1,200 football fields in rural South Carolina, said these moves “run counter to the way American democracy is sold to us.”
“It is a betrayal of everything that this country should stand for, purports to stand for. It runs counter to the will of the people,” he added.
The data center project currently being debated in his 40% Black community was only proposed there after developers tried — and
failed
— to build a
similar campus
in a predominantly white county in Georgia.​
​The change at the federal level would mean that, in some places, residents could lose one of their few formal chances to ask questions, raise alarms, or learn that a data center is headed their way before the permits are signed and construction begins.
In a statement, the EPA said the proposal would “provide the state and local agencies most familiar with local issues the discretion to determine whether, when, and for how long to provide opportunities for public participation.”
But many Americans are increasingly losing faith in their local governments to work in their best interests.
In part of a growing web of secrecy, local governments have routinely signed
nondisclosure agreements
with tech companies to hide these projects and
overruled legal orders
in order to bury information about them.
“What I am saying is that if we, as the community, the people who are responsible, can’t understand this, can’t have questions answered, can’t have information, then how can I look somebody in the eye and tell them this is good for you, trust me?” Davante Lewis, a Louisiana public service commissioner tasked with regulating industry, told Capital B last month.
Lewis was the only member to vote in favor of releasing electricity use information tied to the current construction of the country’s largest data center in rural Louisiana.
Nearly
200 advocacy groups
and more than a dozen states, led by both Democrats and Republicans, have voiced opposition to the federal changes.
Where the biggest threats lie
​“In the more rural parts of the nation, we are under attack by data centers,” Black said. “They are seeking to get in as fast as possible, as quietly as possible, and do what they will to the places [where] we live, that we find precious, the places that we’ve preserved, and they want to come in in the dark of the night to build a data center.”
Last month, South Carolina passed its own
ruling
that says power plants for data centers can be constructed without review or approval from the state’s regulatory commission.
The burden of data center growth is already falling heavily on Black communities. Data centers can
drive demand for gas-fired power plants
and turbines, which emit smog-forming nitrogen oxides, fine particulate matter and, in some cases, hazardous air pollutants such as formaldehyde connected to a slew of cancers.
“It’s beyond cruel for Trump’s EPA to silence front-line communities who bear the brunt of unhealthy air,” said Brandon Jones-Cobb, a senior attorney at the Center for Biological Diversity.

You are comfortable in code: editing the site or wiring an integration. You do not need to have shipped applications.

data.title: CIA Releases President's Daily Briefs in Commemoration of 9/11
data.author: stmw
data.article_summary: 美国中情局于2026年9月11日解密71份总统每日简报及逾100页分析材料，纪念“9·11”事件25周年。这是该机构迄今最大规模的相关解密，内容展示了情报人员在信息有限、模糊的情况下，对“基地”组织及本·拉登袭击阴谋的研判、警告与后续反恐行动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“9·11前情报简报”的公开价值、解读方式及其政治背景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **反对事后归因**：legitster认为，脱离每日大量情报的整体背景，单看少数简报容易“事后挑选”；当时虽担心内战、使馆袭击、生物攻击和欧洲细胞，但对劫机的判断仍可能是换囚等常规事件。  
• **质疑公开动机**：edot认为材料仍有删节，且未说明为何此时发布，因此怀疑其实际意义。  
• **质疑政治叙事**：legitster担心借公开材料攻击前届政府；pbhjpbhj则认为所谓“史无前例的透明度”带有讽刺意味，可能是在转移其他争议。  
• **批评现政府情报处理**：jauntywundrkind指出特朗普不重视每日简报，并称部分情报曾被遗漏；legitster也批评现政府轻视情报。  
• **伊朗议题**：pazimzadeh注意到材料几乎不提伊朗，认为这与当时美国借助伊朗对抗塔利班的背景有关。  
• **阴谋论式质疑**：jijji转向讨论倒计时和“热温压”证据，暗示官方9·11叙事存在疑点。

补充讨论：争议焦点是材料究竟有助于客观复盘，还是被选择性公开并用于政治攻防；评论间也存在对情报缺失、政府责任及9·11成因的不同解释。

49663054.article_content:
CIA Releases President's Daily Briefs in Commemoration of the
25th Anniversary of 9/11
September 11, 2026
For Immediate Release: September 11, 2026
CIA Releases President's Daily Briefs in Commemoration of the
25th Anniversary of 9/11
Agency makes public more than 70 intelligence products in historic release
Today, Director John Ratcliffe declassified
71 President's Daily Brief (PDB) products
in commemoration of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks, and consistent with President Donald Trump's historic transparency initiative.
This collection represents the Agency's single largest release of declassified CIA PDB products related to 9/11, providing unprecedented transparency on America's most sensitive intelligence publication from the years before and the day after one of the darkest moments in our history. The products trace the story of CIA analysts' evolving understanding of al-Qa'ida and efforts to highlight and warn of Usama Bin Ladin's attack plotting despite sparse, vague, and imperfect information.
Under President Trump's leadership, CIA conducted the most thorough declassification effortâunprecedented in size and transparencyâsince the 9/11 Commission's in 2004, resulting in more than 100 pages of CIA analysis that are publicly available for the first time.
"In an act of exceptional transparency, we honor the memory of those we lost on that tragic Tuesday by releasing 71 declassified productsâthe single largest release of CIA analysis related to 9/11 ever," said Director Ratcliffe. "25 years ago, the 9/11 attacks struck a blow to our Nation, but they did not break us. Generations of CIA officers have since dedicated their careers to securing justice for our fallen Americans and ensuring al-Qa'ida would never again harm our country. In the years that followed, numerous CIA officers made the ultimate sacrifice in the Global War on Terror. We honor their memory and service through our commitment to disrupt, dismantle, and defeat those who wish to cause us harm."

data.article_summary: gPTY 是一个基于 Godot 与 Rust 构建的跨平台 PTY 工作台，提供可调整的终端平铺网格、滚屏搜索、文本选择和持久化工作区。它通过 JSON-RPC、CLI 与 MCP 接口支持 AI 代理及自动化工具创建终端、注入文本和观察输出；概念引擎可捕获终端内容并转发至其他面板。项目支持 Linux、macOS、Windows，并提供独立安装包。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“用 Godot 构建现代终端/TTY 多路复用器”是否合理、实用，以及项目表达是否清晰展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持创新者认为，Godot 自带跨平台硬件加速 GUI，编辑器本身就是 Godot 应用，可覆盖 VR、Android、Web 等平台；结合 Rust、WASM 和新推出的 libgodot，能快速交付复杂应用。也有人称赞其突破游戏领域，并表示 tty7 已满足现代终端需求。
• 实用主义者质疑技术选型：Godot 偏单体、体积可能过大，脚本性能和 C++ 开发体验也存在问题；对于二维窗口和文本处理，Chromium/Web、Raylib、Bevy 或 SDL 可能更合适，浏览器的 UI/HUD 能力明显更成熟。
• 强烈反对者认为这是“被 buzzword 推上首页”的无用软件，没看出 Godot 相对传统终端工具的收益，甚至怀疑项目是过度依赖 AI 生成、缺乏真实需求。
• 信息不足的评论者希望增加截图，以及解释“为什么做、为什么现在做”、适用场景和能解决的问题；另有人询问它是否主要用于 agent 自动化或 Godot 应用的端到端测试。

补充讨论：评论还引用了将 Alacritty 嵌入 TeX、Minecraft、Godot 及 Apple 平台的先例，说明技术上并非不可行。争议焦点在于“能否实现”与“是否值得、是否有明确需求”之间的差异；文档过于冗长且带有明显 AI 写作痕迹，也削弱了项目说服力。

gPTY
- a PTY foundation built on Godot and Rust. Provides a tiling grid for panes (terminal, code, file-tree, etc.), a concept capture engine, and a JSON-RPC/MCP control surface so AI agents and automation tools can spawn panes, inject text, and observe output on terminals without scraping a TUI.
Overview
PTY
- Spawn and manage independent shell sessions in a resizable tiling grid. Full
DEC STD 070
via
alacritty_terminal
:
16
/
256
/
true color
, scrollback with regex search, wrapped text selection.
Public API
- JSON-RPC IPC socket + CLI (
gpty new-pane
,
gpty inject
, …) + MCP server. AI agents, scripts, and orchestrators drive the workspace over a documented, versioned protocol.
Concept engine
- RegEx triggers on PTY output capture the reply and route it into adjacent panes (code viewer, Inspector). Write your own or ship the defaults. Concepts capture and display only - they never inject input into a shell.
Agent observability
- Reasoning pane passively projects documented agent lifecycle events (OMP, extensible); Inspector pane runs a private, tool-free Q&A session. Observability only - gpty never orchestrates agent state.
Persistence
- Scrollback, settings, workspaces (named tab sets), and profiles auto-save to SQLite/JSON and restore on restart; full-text search across each pane's persisted history.
Cross-platform
- Standalone binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows. No Godot or Rust toolchain required to run.
Documentation
-
https://godot-pty.github.io/gpty/
The vast majority of this codebase, including most of the Godot UI layout and the Rust (
gpty-core
) GDExtension bridge, was generated using LLMs; and as such, the underlying code may contain unidiomatic patterns and/or bugs.
Component
Choice
Rationale
PTY library
portable-pty
Cross-platform (Linux
/dev/ptmx
+ Windows ConPTY) with a single API
ANSI parsing
vte
crate
Fast Rust ANSI state machine
Async runtime
tokio
Per-terminal tasks; channel-driven capture state machine
I/O threading
Dedicated
std::thread
per PTY
Predictable blocking reads; bridges to tokio via
mpsc
Concept capture
Rust
regex
over parsed
LineParser
output
Linear-time matching (ReDoS-safe); captures buffer raw bytes for grid-faithful replay
Grid rendering
alacritty_terminal
Full DEC STD 070 grid state machine; pass arrays to Godot
_draw()
Godot bridge
gdext 0.5
Native GDExtension for Godot 4.7+
Rust edition
2024
Requires Rust >= 1.85
Installation & Usage
Standalone binaries (no Godot install required) are published on
GitHub Releases
for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Platform
Package
Linux
gpty-v0.5.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
- extract;
./gpty-gui.sh
starts the GUI,
./gpty
is the CLI
macOS
gpty-v0.5.3-macos.zip
- unzip, right-click the
.app
→ Open;
gpty
beside it is the CLI
Windows
gpty-v0.5.3-windows-x86_64.zip
- unzip;
gpty-gui.exe
starts the GUI,
gpty.exe
is the CLI
Each release publishes a
SHA256SUMS
listing every asset. Check the file you downloaded before running it:
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
#
Linux
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
#
macOS
certutil -hashfile
<
asset
>
SHA256
#
Windows
Checksums catch a corrupted or tampered download in transit; they are not a signature - release artifacts are unsigned (see
SECURITY.md
).
CLI
The
gpty
binary controls a running GUI over JSON-RPC IPC, and every release bundle ships it next to the GUI, which it starts on demand (
--no-daemon
opts out). Building from source (
cargo build -p gpty
, or
cargo build --workspace
) is only needed when working on the CLI itself.
Once the GUI is running (launched from Godot or a release binary), the CLI connects over a Unix socket (
$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gpty.sock
on Linux, or
GPTY_SOCKET
env var):
#
Check if the GUI is running
gpty version
#
Print the bundled agent skill (for coding agents running inside a pane)
gpty --skill
#
Spawn a new terminal pane
gpty new-pane --pane-type terminal
#
List all active panes
gpty list-panes
#
Send text to a pane (by label, e.g. T1)
gpty inject T1 --text
"
echo hello
"
#
Close a pane
gpty kill-pane T1
#
Save and load named layouts
gpty layout save my-setup
gpty layout load my-setup
gpty layout list
#

data.title: How the Chorleywood Bread Process transformed British bread
data.author: baud147258
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国面包工业化、面粉品质与传统烘焙之间的关系，以及供应链、本土产业和消费者口味的取舍。

不同观点：
• 支持现代工艺者认为，乔利伍德面包工艺通过机械充气、缩短发酵时间和提高生产效率，降低了成本；现代高蛋白面粉也使高含水量的恰巴塔等面包更易制作。  
• 批评者认为该工艺制造出松软、寡淡、易压缩的“工业面包”，并使真正的面包变得昂贵、难以获得；还有人指出超加工食品可能与肠易激综合征有关。  
• 有人质疑文章过度简化：英国育种已提高本土小麦蛋白质含量，市售“强力面粉”多为英国小麦；11%蛋白质的普通面粉也能制作恰巴塔。  
• 面包师关注实际选择：进口加拿大面粉效果更稳定，但使用英国小麦有助于支持本土企业，只是需要更多技术调整。  
• 消费者体验存在地域差异：部分欧洲评论者普遍认为英美面包难吃，并追问法国长棍面包优异是否源于小麦品种、面筋含量或制作方法。  
• 另有观点认为，餐饮中过厚、过干的海绵状面包影响口感，甚至可能促成对面包或麸质的排斥。

补充讨论：评论也涉及全球供应链依赖、本地生产与效率的冲突；部分人批评原文铺垫冗长、论述分散，削弱了文章说服力。

data.title: How we rebuilt complex permissions without migrating to Zanzibar
data.author: FinnLobsien
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Infisical 推出基于文件夹的访问控制，以弥补传统 RBAC 难以处理“额外授权”和“权限收回”的不足。原有 Additional Privileges 配置复杂、容易误配，且依赖路径字符串，重命名文件夹会失效。新方案通过文件夹 ID 管理权限，更直观、稳定，但由于系统中存在用户、机器身份、群组等多种授权来源，实施过程相当复杂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：企业软件中的授权系统设计，以及自研方案与专用授权系统之间的取舍。

不同观点：
• [jzelinskie] 认可文章对授权重要性的强调，也理解企业本地部署场景下减少依赖的考虑。工程师应根据实际情况决定继续自研还是采用专用系统；该设计与 Zanzibar/SpiceDB 的理念相似，未来迁移到专用方案会相对容易。  
• [jzelinskie] 指出文章遗漏了一个代价：自研方案通常缺少专用系统提供的调试、正确性验证及 CI/CD 工具链，这会增加维护成本和风险。  
• [peterldowns] 直接质疑为何不采用 Zanzibar，代表倾向使用成熟专用授权系统的立场。  
• [Synthetic7346] 认为安全功能乃至安全团队往往只有在缺失时才会被注意到，强调其价值常常是“隐形”的。  
• [knob] 认为 RBAC 虽必要却不够吸引人，但文章仍提供了有价值的实践 insight。

补充讨论：评论整体认可授权和安全基础设施的重要性，争议焦点集中在自研的部署便利与可控性，和专用系统在成熟度、工具链及长期可维护性之间的权衡。CASL.js 链接问题已被修复。

49635043.article_content:
I recently built a simple feature most customers might never notice as a complex bit of engineering: Infisical users can now grant/deny access to single folders. This is the kind of thing that gets a brief mention in the all-hands and a one-line changelog entry.
RBAC, permissions, and authorization are the same class of engineering project as billing, schema migrations, and audit logs:
They're expected utilities
Users spend as little time on them as possible
They're tricky engineering projects, even when they look simple
The best case is no complaints and that the system is correct. It can never excel. There's no 10x RBAC system people rave about on Twitter. Access controls are a box a product checks, but not a killer feature.
That doesn’t make them less important. Enterprise buyers will never sign an order form without them. And in
secrets management
(one of the categories Infisical operates in), getting access wrong means someone sees credentials they shouldn't, or a customer’s deployment fails at three in the morning because a service lost access to a secret.
Tailscale
and
Oso
have both written about why authorization is harder than it looks. Building folder-based access taught me the same thing from a different direction.
Why we built folder access
Conceptually, RBAC is simple. Each identity, human or machine, has a role (e.g.
admin
,
member
, or
guest
) which carries permissions:
Actions:
What you can do
Subjects:
What you can take the actions on.
We use
CASL
, in which a basic permission attached to a role can look something like this:
JSON
Copy
{
"action": ["readValue", "create"],
"subject": "secrets",
"conditions": { "environment": "staging" }
}
This identity can read and create secrets in staging environments. CASL automatically denies anything not explicitly allowed. A role with the permission above could never touch secrets in production environments.
Role-based access is popular because humans intuitively get it. Roles in RBAC map to roles in teams, and granting/denying privileges in bulk saves time compared to manually setting permissions for each team member, which would turn access controls into a full-time job.
But not all access control changes perfectly match roles. There are two special cases for why we built folder-based access:
Take an engineer who is the only one on his team with Netsuite experience, so they’ve
been condemned to
earned the privilege of building the Netsuite integration.
They need the
engineer
role’s credentials plus Netsuite credentials.
Other cases require stripping a given role of a privilege. A specialist contractor brought in to refactor AWS Lambda functions needs engineering credentials, but there’s no reason to let them see financial data.
They need the
engineer
role’s credentials minus billing credentials.
In both of these cases, someone’s role doesn’t change, but their access requirements do. Solving this with conventional RBAC gives us two dissatisfying options:
Editing the
engineer
role grants unnecessary access or takes necessary access away.
Creating a modified custom role based on
engineer
creates parallel configuration for a one-off use case and might lead to drift.
At Infisical, we had a third option called Additional Privileges, which folder-based RBAC is now replacing. It was a per-person grant that sits on top of a role. It worked, but was too convoluted (it showed every possible permission you could possibly grant) and could not subtract privileges.
This was powerful, but not intuitive. It required understanding every Infisical concept, our data hierarchy, and that specific instance’s setup. We can’t assume this of every user, so additional privileges risked two failure modes:
Users could misconfigure the privileges they wanted to provision and provide too much or too little access.
Users could say “I don’t have time for that” and grant broader access, which would compromise their security posture.
Additional privileges also stored paths as strings, and renaming a folder broke them. Folders have a
folderID
UUID, which means renaming a folder or moving it from one environment to another won’t break the folder-based access grant.
We needed a solution that was intuitive to users. Folders were the right place because we ship no default folder structure. If a folder exists, users know why and what’s in it, because they put it there. Folder-based RBAC simplifies the translation of the access problem in the user’s mind to a configuration in Infisical.
The user-facing outcome is simpler, but the engineering work was complex because we couldn’t just extend our existing model.
Why our RBAC system was too complex to extend
We couldn’t add yet another way to grant access that only works for folders because there are already many ways someone may have access to a secret. Here are just a few ways to define access in Infisical:
A user can be a member of a project directly, and so can a machine identity.
A group can hold the membership instead and contain both human

• [jzelinskie] 认可文章对授权重要性的强调，也理解企业本地部署场景下减少依赖的考虑。工程师应根据实际情况决定继续自研还是采用专用系统；该设计与 Zanzibar/SpiceDB 的理念相似，未来迁移到专用方案会相对容易。

data.title: Show HN: Bodily Oddities
data.author: vesterde
data.article_summary: 《Bodily Oddities》介绍人体可能出现的各种奇特现象，涵盖大脑、神经、眼睛、耳朵、肌肉、骨骼、心脏等部位，并按感知、反射、非自主动作、生理变异等分类。文章解释了幻觉、耳垂形态、眼后残像、肌肉跳动、胸前刺痛等现象，说明其发生比例及成因，强调许多看似可怕的表现其实正常且无害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“身体奇异体验”网站展开分享，涉及视觉、听觉、平衡、神经反应及健康焦虑等现象。

不同观点：
• 视觉现象：有人描述飞蚊症、运动后看到发光“蠕虫”、凝视后的灰视与干涉图案，以及闭眼听到巨响时看到闪光；也有人提到可感知偏振光（Haidinger’s brush）。
• 睡眠与感知异常：有人童年发烧或极度疲劳时出现几何图形噩梦；有人醒来时听到逼真的门铃声（催眠后幻觉），但家人并未听见。
• 生理反射与能力：光喷嚏反射可能影响战斗机飞行员筛选，且有人伴随连续喷嚏和先天嗅觉缺失；另有人能主动动耳，甚至带动头皮。
• 疼痛、眩晕与身体感受：评论涉及短暂神经电击感、突发胸痛、冬季躺下时眩晕、短暂肛门痉挛，以及看到他人坠落或接近高处时脚底产生下坠感。
• 内容补充建议：建议加入似曾相识的反面“ jamais vu”、脸盲症和耳石症等条目。
• 网站质量争议：多数人称赞创意和内容，但有人批评 AI 生成图片中的手部畸形、手指数量错误，影响观感。

补充讨论：部分评论强调这些体验通常并不代表疾病；但也有人因网络自诊容易把所有症状联想到癌症，表示相关内容可能诱发健康焦虑。作者回应称会根据反馈补充和修订网站。

data.author: ninju

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：铜锌背心用于帮助受伤企鹅愈合的医学依据、历史渊源及其是否适用于人类。

不同观点：
• [adrian_b]指出铜、锌并非全新疗法。古希腊罗马时期已使用氧化锌、碱式碳酸铜制作药膏；黄铜冶炼产生的氧化锌，以及铜器表面的绿色腐蚀物，都曾被收集入药。  
• [derefr]关注实际应用，询问人类医学中是否有类似做法，例如使用含铜锌的水胶体敷料，暗示这种疗法可能具有推广价值。  
• [willis936]持怀疑态度，认为该“奇迹疗法”只在动物身上实施，可能是因为动物医学监管和法律保护较弱，并以“离子化珠宝”作为疑似伪科学的类比。  
• [ninju]以幽默方式评论，认为穿背心比其他宠物戴“羞耻圈”更时髦，主要关注外观和趣味性。  
• [photonemitter]的方言式短句似乎是在调侃“给它穿上锌背心”，态度偏戏谑，但含义不完全明确。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于铜锌材料是否真正能促进伤口愈合，以及动物试验结果能否支持医学推广。历史上的药用记录说明材料并非毫无依据，但不能直接证明现代背心疗法有效。

data.title: Google will buy half the electricity from one of Finland's nuclear power plants
data.author: lukaspetersson
data.article_summary: 谷歌宣布在芬兰投资130亿欧元，建设三个新数据中心、扩建现有设施，并支持清洁能源项目，以满足人工智能服务需求。公司还与芬兰电力企业签署22年协议，购买洛维萨核电站最多一半电力。该项目预计创造超过3.7万个建设岗位，并推动芬兰经济增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google在芬兰建设数据中心并与Fortum签署长期核电采购协议，引发对低碳能源、基础设施、税收贡献及电力市场影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为芬兰、瑞典、挪威拥有低排放电力、寒冷气候和较少拥堵的电网，适合数据中心；芬兰较低电价和冷却成本也能惠及客户。  
• 怀疑者认为该协议主要是锁定低价和公关行为，并未真正新增电力基础设施；Loviisa核电站本来也会继续运行，除非政府补贴低于每千瓦时15欧分的价格。  
• 有人担忧Google在北欧的用电规模巨大，瑞典规划最高达3.5GW，可能挤占本地及邻国电力、推高价格，减少原本可出口的 surplus。  
• 批评者质疑其公共收益：相关芬兰公司近年几乎不缴企业税，仅有约120名直接员工，增值税贡献也有限。  
• 环保与监管观点要求证明“额外性”：购买既有核电是否真的增加清洁能源；评论提到美国亚马逊类似协议曾因成本转嫁给其他用户而被否决。  
• 另一种观点认为欧洲缺电，应借此推动新建或扩建核电。  
• 也有人怀疑未来模型压缩和硬件效率提升后，5至10年是否仍需要如此多的数据中心和能源。

补充讨论：核废料、AI需求增长与能源效率之间存在明显争议；寒冷气候可降低冷却成本，但大型数据中心的长期用电需求及其市场外部性仍缺乏共识。

49652105.article_content:
Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe
2 days ago
Share
Save
Add as preferred on Google
Jessica Rawnsley
Getty Images
Google will buy up to half the electricity produced by one of Finland's nuclear power plants as part of a record €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) investment in the country's AI infrastructure, the company announced.
The US tech giant said the package would fund three new data centres, expand an existing site and support energy projects to power growing demand for AI services.
"This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," the company said on Wednesday.
"Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a statement.
As part of the deal, Google signed a 22-year contract with Finnish utility Fortum to buy up to 50% of the output from the Loviisa nuclear power plant.
Earlier this week, TikTok announced a $1bn investment in Finland to build a new data centre in Kouvola, pointing to the country's "strong digital infrastructure, clean energy mix, robust data governance and skilled tech talent".
Finland has emerged as an attractive location for data centres because of its cool climate, plentiful low-carbon electricity and relatively uncongested power grid. The colder temperatures can reduce the energy needed to cool facilities packed with computer servers.
Technology companies are racing to secure power supplies as the AI boom drives demand for vast networks of data centres.
The Google investment is expected to support more than 37,000 jobs during construction and boost Finland's GDP by €3.6bn a year, according to Google. Construction is set to take place in 2027 and 2028.
"The value of the data economy extends far beyond direct investment into spurring innovation, research and development," Orpo added.
"Deepening our collaboration with Google will deliver lasting benefits for both parties."
Google will build new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala, while expanding its existing facility in Hamina, which it established after converting a former paper mill in 2009.
The infrastructure will help support products such as its AI chatbot Gemini, alongside services including Search, Maps and YouTube.
Google said the investments also covered "clean energy projects, and dedicated nature and community funds to support local biodiversity, education, research, and workforce development".
"Google is proud to deepen our roots in Finland," said Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and Google.
"This investment underscores Google's commitment to grow our presence responsibly, pairing the expansion of our technical infrastructure with new energy capacity, grid enhancements, and energy affordability initiatives," she added.
Earlier this year, Google's parent company Alphabet raised its global spending plans to as much as $205bn as it sought to expand computing capacity for AI services.
The agreement with Fortum provides long-term financial certainty for the Loviisa plant, which currently generates about 10% of Finland's electricity.
Fortum said Google's commitment would support an investment programme aimed at extending the life of the nuclear station and increasing its generating capacity.

• 环保与监管观点要求证明“额外性”：购买既有核电是否真的增加清洁能源；评论提到美国亚马逊类似协议曾因成本转嫁给其他用户而被否决。  
• 另一种观点认为欧洲缺电，应借此推动新建或扩建核电。  
• 也有人怀疑未来模型压缩和硬件效率提升后，5至10年是否仍需要如此多的数据中心和能源。

补充讨论：核废料、AI需求增长与能源效率之间存在明显争议；寒冷气候可降低冷却成本，但大型数据中心的长期用电需求及其市场外部性仍缺乏共识。

TL;DR
An AI software factory is five stages with a gate at each one. The agent is the cheap part.

The short version: every company that made this work built the gates before the fleet. Spotify's
Fleetshift
shipped in 2023, two years before it had an agent to put in it. Generation scales with spend, review does not, and that asymmetry is the whole design problem.
Where

Agents need live web context the repo does not carry.

for the open web and a curated
developer index
for code, both behind

prompt injection detection
on every fetch.
On January 6, 2026,
Stephen Toub
opened nine pull requests from his phone at 35,000 feet. Seven of them merged. He works on
dotnet/runtime
, and he
wrote up what the experience told him
:
AI changes the economics of code production. One person with good judgment and a phone can generate PRs faster than a team can review them.
That sentence is the entire subject. A single engineer with a coding agent can now saturate a team's review capacity from an airplane seat. The interesting question stopped being how to make agents write code and became how to absorb the output.
An AI software factory is the answer companies have converged on, and it is what turns autonomous coding agents from a demo into throughput a team can absorb. This guide breaks it into five stages, each with the published architecture behind it and the configuration to build it. For the broader picture of how
AI agents
reason, call tools, and pull in web context, start with that primer, then come back here for how a coding-agent fleet actually gets shipped.
Assume you have already picked an agent, which we covered in our roundup of the
best AI coding agents
. The software factory is everything around it.
What is an AI software factory?
An AI software factory is the system around a coding agent rather than the agent itself. Work arrives from a queue, agents run in isolated workspaces, verification happens automatically, and a human sits at an explicit merge gate. Also called an agentic software factory.
The useful distinction is between an agent and a software factory. Running a coding agent on your laptop is an agent: you choose the task, you watch it work, you read the diff, you merge. Everything except the typing is still you, and your attention is the limit.
A software factory moves those steps into infrastructure. Nobody decides which issue an agent picks up, because intake rules do. Nobody sets up a workspace, because isolation is provisioned. Nobody checks whether the change compiles, because verification runs before a human is involved at all. The person shows up at the end, on the decisions that carry accountability.
Addy Osmani
puts it more compactly
:
A software factory is harnessing loops at scale.
The loops he means are the ones we covered in our guide to
loop engineering
: an agent that runs, checks its own work, and runs again until a verifier says stop. The software factory is the machinery that runs many of them at once without anyone watching.
Three properties separate a real software factory from a pile of scripts:
It is queue-driven, not prompt-driven.
Work enters from issues, alerts, or a Slack channel, and the system decides what is worth starting. Nobody is typing prompts.
Environments are disposable.
Every agent gets a clean workspace it can destroy, so a bad run costs nothing and parallel runs cannot corrupt each other.
Verification runs before review.
By the time a diff reaches a person, it has already compiled, passed tests, and been checked for scope.
Miss the third and you have not built a software factory. You have built a machine that generates review work faster than you can absorb it, which is the failure mode the rest of this article is organized around avoiding.
